reviewEvidence:
Approved against revision-616b9536, the final sealed revision of this task. The change closes the three gaps a
command-routing assessment named — host-run visibility, a reverse routing guard, and a container picker — and it
has been reviewed by TWENTY-TWO independent fresh-context adversarial passes (per-revision passes plus the kata
verify and review nodes, each bound to a frozen brief and recorded through the adversarial gate), across 16 sealed
revisions. Roughly seventy findings were raised and every one was either fixed in code or recorded as a
deliberate, documented limitation.

WHAT IT DELIVERS
- AC-1: the session's host-command attempt count and the programs it named are visible in `/devcontainer status`,
  and the first attempt is announced on the operator channel, with an honest statement of whether a record was
  written. No command text is stored or rendered: every surface (the ledger, the runner's notice and the WITHHELD
  path's notice) renders through one enforced `displayProgram` — the first whitespace-delimited token of argv[0],
  redacted with the audit rules, then reduced to the HOST of whatever the token looks like, control characters
  stripped, capped at 64, never blank — because a program name CAN be credential-shaped and argv[0] CAN be a whole
  command line. The audit trail remains the authoritative record.
- AC-2/AC-3: `devcontainer_exec` refuses an argv element that names the HOST workspace path when the configuration
  maps it elsewhere, with a typed `policy-denied` naming the container path to use, audited as a denial with command
  identity; skipped with no mapping, for a same-path mapping, and for a container path nested under the host path.
  The match is path identity at a real segment boundary (root included) and deliberately does not inspect routed
  shell text.
- AC-4: `/devcontainer use` offers a container picker (id, state, image) from both entry points and binds exactly
  the picked candidate INCLUDING its own state; candidates are ordered running-first, so Docker's listing order
  never decides.
- AC-5: the host-escape gating asymmetry is documented as deliberate, with its reasoning, the compensating controls
  and the exact scope of the audit-side redaction; a withheld attempt is documented as never reaching the runner.
- AC-6: no regression — the CLI still receives the HOST workspace path, no argv shape changed, discovery stays
  lazy/read-only/bounded, targets are never auto-started, `stop`/`remove` keep both gates, host execution stays
  withheld-able with unchanged operation/initiator/capture defaults, `/devcontainer setup` is untouched, and the
  audit shape and modes are unchanged.

WHAT THE REVIEWS BOUGHT (they all shipped fixed)
Blocking/major findings, in the order they were found: the picker was unreachable when the ambiguous workspace was
not the only match; the operator notice and the ledger could render a credential (four separate leaks); the reverse
guard's refusal was audited as an authorized run; a withheld attempt was invisible on the agent's surface; the
guard refused legitimate work (mirror mounts, a root host path, a nested container path); `selectionFor` took its
state from the wrong candidate; the guard's mapping read failed unaudited; two redaction compositions were
non-monotone; a scheme-less credential-shaped argv[0] rendered its password; Docker's listing order could decide the
target; and — found twice, independently — the withheld notice interpolated a raw argv element, a leak the previous
fix had introduced. Six of those were the same failure mode: a fix applied to one surface and not its mirror, which
is why the segment predicate now exists exactly once (`isAtOrUnder`/`isSamePath`) and every rendering goes through
one enforced function.

REMAINING (recorded, none blocking; a scoped follow-up task)
The 23 items in `.kata/tasks/routing-hardening/wiki/` include one regression introduced by the last nit fix
(`hostToContainer` with a root host path), two documentation sentences that overstate the residual redaction scope,
the unknown-verb diagnostic interpolating raw input, a bare `host-exec` counting as an attempt, `tsconfig` not
covering `tests/**`, and the docs still pinning `@devcontainers/cli@0.88.0` while the host resolves 0.89.0. None
affects the behaviours above.

findings.message: hostToContainer's new delegation to the shared predicate inherits the root special case but not a matching join, so a mapping whose host path is `/` now returns a mangled container path instead of no mapping. `hostToContainer("/a/b", {hostPath:"/", containerPath:"/x"})` returns `/xa/b` (missing separator); the pre-revision body returned undefined for the same input because it tested `candidate.startsWith(`${host}/`)` (i.e. `//`). Reachable: readConfigFacts accepts `"workspaceMount": "source=/,target=/x,type=bind"` (both sides absolute) -> buildPathMapping -> {hostPath:'/', containerPath:'/x'}, and extensions/index.ts:280 (resolveContainerWorkspace) feeds the value into ExecOutcome.workspaceKey, i.e. the workspace path the tool reports to the model. The same root rule also makes containerOnlyMounts treat every mount target as already covered when the workspace container path is `/`.

docs/security.md:171 states a narrower residual scope than the renderer implements, in the one paragraph that is supposed to be the exact non-absolute scope. It says a credential can only reach the operator surfaces "by being spelled as a program NAME with no `@` or `/` at all (`argv[0]="hunter2"`)", but displayProgram(["host@QWERTY42"]) -> "QWERTY42" and displayProgram(["/tmp/QWERTY42"]) -> "QWERTY42", i.e. the credential also reaches the surfaces as the segment after the last `@` or as the basename of a path. The sentence immediately before it ("renders the HOST of whatever that token looks like") is accurate; the gloss that follows overstates the protection.

The change's headline feature (AC-1, host-run visibility) is absent from both READMEs while the other two behaviour changes of the same revision are documented there. README.md:209 still describes `/devcontainer status` as "Same status block (target, registry, route, caps)", but renderStatus now also prints `host runs: N host command attempts this session — most recent: ...`; grep for "host runs"/"host command attempts"/"尝试" finds no mention of the visibility in README.md or README.zh-CN.md, although the reverse guard and the container picker were added to both (README.md:215-216, README.zh-CN.md:154-155). CHANGELOG.md and docs/security.md do cover it.

The scheme-less `@` branch added by the rev-16 fix applies to every token containing an `@`, including an absolute path whose directory contains one, so a credential-free path does not keep its basename (AC-1's rendering spec) and the visibility can name a program that is not the one being run: displayProgram(["/opt/app@2/dist/bin/tool"]) -> "2" and displayProgram(["/usr/lib/node_modules/@babel/cli/bin/babel.js"]) -> "babel". The pre-revision body returned "tool" and "babel.js" (its @-branch only fired when the first `/`-segment contained an @), so this is a fidelity regression introduced by the fix that closed the real leak - the safe direction for credentials, but it degrades the very signal the ledger exists to provide.

docs/security.md:188 says a withheld attempt "is visible only through the in-session summary", which the code contradicts and the same paragraph contradicts two lines later. extensions/index.ts:565-573 announces the FIRST withheld attempt of a session through ctx.ui.notify ("first host command attempt this session: <program> ... no audit record"), and the following clause of the same sentence says "the first of a session is announced on the operator channel". The honest note the claim requires (a withheld attempt never reaches the runner) is present; only the word "only" is wrong.

src/runtime/host-discovery.ts:356-357 still reads "Expose EVERY candidate, ordered by Docker's own listing (which puts the running container first), and fail closed when more than one is running so result order never decides the target" directly above the `.sort((l,r) => Number(r.state==='running') - Number(l.state==='running'))` that was added precisely because that Docker assumption was false (the rev-14 major: a stopped container listed first became a workspace's primary candidate). The comment now states the opposite of the enforced invariant.

docs/security.md's 'What the redaction covers, and what it does not' paragraph states that the in-session rendering 'renders the HOST of whatever that token looks like - the authority between `://` and the first `/` (its userinfo dropped)', that the redaction gaps 'matter only under "redacted-text"', and that a credential 'can therefore only reach the operator surfaces by being spelled as a program NAME with no `@` or `/` at all ..., which is not a shape a command line produces in practice'. The renderer emits the pre-slash authority VERBATIM whenever that authority contains no `@`, so a URL-shaped argv[0] with a credential in front of a slash (or with no `@` in the authority at all) puts the credential pair on BOTH operator surfaces under the DEFAULT capture mode (fingerprint-only, no command text recorded): displayProgram(["https://alice:hunter2/@db.example.test"]) === "alice:hunter2", displayProgram(["x@y://alice:hunter2"]) === "alice:hunter2", displayProgram(["postgres://admin:P/w0rd@db.internal"]) === "admin:P" (the slash-in-the-password shape the paragraph itself calls out), displayProgram(["deployer@db.example.test:hunter2"]) === "db.example.test:hunter2"; the leaked value appears in `/devcontainer status` via the ledger and in the one-shot withheld/runner notice. The rendered string is always @-less and /-less (0 of 32768 brute-forced tokens produced a render containing either character), so the code matches AC-1's own definition of the render (the authority between `://` and the first `/`) and this is a documentation-accuracy defect rather than a renderer regression: the paragraph's 'renders the HOST', 'matter only under redacted-text' and 'not a shape a command line produces in practice' clauses need narrowing (or the renderer needs to shave a `user:pass`-shaped authority). The same overstatement appears in CHANGELOG.md ('without creating a place a credential could be rendered'), while src/host-run-ledger.ts itself concedes the truth ('a program name CAN be credential-shaped').

The nit fix in b02dadf ('hostToContainer still hand-rolled the prefix math - the last private segment implementation. It delegates to the shared predicate now') changed behaviour for a mapping whose host side is the filesystem root. hostToContainer('/etc/passwd', {hostPath:'/', containerPath:'/workspaces/proj'}) now returns '/workspaces/projetc/passwd': the root base passes isAtOrUnder, but `${mapping.containerPath}${candidate.slice(host.length)}` (src/path-mapper.ts:103) then slices off the leading separator and the container path has no trailing slash to spare ('/workspaces/proj' + 'etc/passwd'). The pre-revision implementation (git show 8e6b491:src/path-mapper.ts, executed inline) returned undefined for the same call, i.e. 'no mapping' - the safe answer that leaves the host path unchanged. Reachability is narrow but real: buildPathMapping accepts workspaceMount 'source=/,target=/workspace,type=bind' (or a config at /.devcontainer/devcontainer.json), the codebase itself treats {hostPath:'/'} as a legitimate mapping (tests/unit/routing-guards.test.ts:310), and no test covers hostToContainer with a root host side. Impact is presentation-only rather than a routing decision: extensions/index.ts:280 resolveContainerWorkspace feeds ExecOutcome.presentedWorkspace, so a root-mounted workspace at /srv/proj is shown to the agent as '/workspacesrv/proj'. The guard predicate stays shared; only the join needs the root case handled (or path-segment joining instead of a slice).

The only operator-channel surface in this change's blast radius that still interpolates raw input is the unknown-verb diagnostic: extensions/index.ts:715 (dist/extensions/index.js:592) notifies `Unknown /devcontainer verb: ${verb}` with `verb` being the raw first token of the command arguments (lowercased). Every neighbouring surface now routes through the enforced renderer (the withheld notice at extensions/index.ts:571, the free-text refusal at src/commands.ts:836), so a token of exactly the shape this change is about (e.g. `/devcontainer https://alice:hunter2@host`) is echoed verbatim here. It is the operator's own typing and pre-existing (not introduced by this revision), hence a nit - but it is the one remaining raw echo, and `displayProgram([verb])` (or a static message naming the verb picker) would close it.

On the WITHHELD path a bare `/devcontainer host-exec` with no argv is counted as a host-command attempt and can consume the session's one-shot first-attempt notice: src/commands.ts:694-698 calls onWithheldHostAttempt(parseHostExecArgv(args).ok ? argv[0] : args.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] ?? "") before any grammar check, so `args === ""` yields the empty program, the ledger counts 1 and the notice reads 'first host command attempt this session: (no command)'. The same invocation with host execution ALLOWED is not an attempt at all (parseHostExecArgv fails, the usage text is returned, no ledger call, no runner), and the tool surface cannot produce it because argv declares minItems: 1 (src/tools.ts:44) - so the slash-command path over-reports the AC-1 attempt count exactly where a configuration withholds the surface. Cheap fix: treat a failing parse with empty args like the allowed path (usage, no count).
